Ibn Shihab said: 'Umar ibn Thabit al-Ansari informed me that some companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said on the day he warned the people of the Dajjal: 'Indeed, written between his eyes is Kafir, which whoever despises his deeds will read—or every believer will read.' And he said: 'Know that none of you will ever see his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, until he dies.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2930 b, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ ابْنِ صَيَّادٍ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الْحُلْوَانِيُّ، وَعَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا يَعْقُوبُ، - وَهُوَ ابْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ - حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، عَنْ صَالِحٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي سَالِمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، أَنَّالله عليه وسلم وَمَعَهُ رَهْطٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فِيهِمْ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ حَتَّى وَجَدَ ابْنَ صَيَّادٍ غُلاَمًا قَدْ نَاهَزَ الْحُلُمَ يَلْعَبُ مَعَ الْغِلْمَانِ عِنْدَ أُطُمِ بَنِي مُعَاوِيَةَ ‏.‏ وَسَاقَ الْحَدِيثَ بِمِثْلِ حَدِيثِ يُونُسَ إِلَى مُنْتَهَى حَدِيثِ عُمَرَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ قَالَ أُبَىٌّ - يَعْنِي فِي قَوْلِهِ لَوْ تَرَكَتْهُ بَيَّنَ - قَالَ لَوْ تَرَكَتْهُ أُمُّهُ بَيَّنَ أَمْرَهُ ‏.‏
en_text: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Ya'qub—and he is Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Salim ibn 'Abdullah informed me that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar informed him that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab set out with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), accompanied by a group of his companions among whom was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, until he found Ibn Sayyad as a boy approaching puberty playing with the boys near the fortress of Banu Mu'awiyah... and he conveyed the hadith like the hadith of Yunus up to the end of the hadith of 'Umar ibn Thabit. And in the hadith from Ya'qub he said: Ubayy said—meaning regarding his saying 'If she had left him alone, he would have made it clear'—he said: 'If his mother had left him alone, his case would have become clear.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2930 c, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ ابْنِ صَيَّادٍ
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، وَسَلَمَةُ بْنُ شَبِيبٍ، جَمِيعًا عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّزَّاقِ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ سَالِمٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَرَّ بِابْنِ صَيَّادٍ فِي نَفَرٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فِيهِمْ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ وَهُوَ يَلْعَبُ مَعَ الْغِلْمَانِ عِنْدَ أُطُمِ بَنِي مَغَالَةَ وَهُوَ غُلاَمٌ ‏.‏ بِمَعْنَى حَدِيثِ يُونُسَ وَصَالِحٍ غَيْرَ أَنَّ عَبْدَ بْنَ حُمَيْدٍ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ حَدِيثَ ابْنِ عُمَرَ فِي انْطِلاَقِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَعَ أُبَىِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ إِلَى النَّخْلِ ‏.‏
en_text: And 'Abd ibn Humayd and Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, both from 'Abd ar-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed by Ibn Sayyad along with a group of his companions among whom was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, while he was playing with the boys near the fortress of Banu Maghalah, and he was a young boy... with the meaning of the hadith of Yunus and Salih, except that 'Abd ibn Humayd did not mention the hadith of Ibn 'Umar regarding the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) going with Ubayy ibn Ka'b to the date palms.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2932 a, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ ابْنِ صَيَّادٍ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا رَوْحُ بْنُ عُبَادَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، قَالَ لَقِيَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ ابْنَ صَائِدٍ فِي بَعْضِ طُرُقِ الْمَدِينَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ قَوْلاً أَغْضَبَهُ فَانْتَفَخَ حَتَّى مَلأَ السِّكَّةَ فَدَخَلَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ عَلَى حَفْصَةَ وَقَدْ بَلَغَهَا فَقَالَتْ لَهُ رَحِمَكَ اللَّهُ مَا أَرَدْتَ مِنِ ابْنِ صَائِدٍ أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْ غَضْبَةٍ يَغْضَبُهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', who said: Ibn 'Umar met Ibn Sa'id in one of the alleys of Medina and said something to him that angered him, so he swelled up until he filled the entire alleyway. Ibn 'Umar then entered upon Hafsah, who had already heard of it, and she said to him: 'May Allah have mercy on you! What did you want with Ibn Sa'id? Did you not know that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "He will only emerge out of anger that enrages him"?'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2932 b, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ ابْنِ صَيَّادٍ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، حَدَّثَنَا حُسَيْنٌ، - يَعْنِي ابْنَ حَسَنِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ - حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ، عَوْنٍ عَنْ نَافِعٍ، قَالَ كَانَ نَافِعٌ يَقُولُ ابْنُ صَيَّادٍ ‏.‏ قَالَ قَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ لَقِيتُهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ - قَالَ - فَلَقِيتُهُ فَقُلْتُ لِبَعْضِهِمْ هَلْ تَحَدَّثُونَ أَنَّهُ هُوَ قَالَ لاَ وَاللَّهِ - قَالَ - قُلْتُ كَذَبْتَنِي وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَخْبَرَنِي بَعْضُكُمْ أَنَّهُ لَنْ يَمُوتَ حَتَّى يَكُونَ أَكْثَرَكُمْ مَالاً وَوَلَدًا فَكَذَلِكَ هُوَ زَعَمُوا الْيَوْمَ - قَالَ - فَتَحَدَّثْنَا ثُمَّ فَارَقْتُهُ - قَالَ - فَلَقِيتُهُ لَقْيَةً أُخْرَى وَقَدْ نَفَرَتْ عَيْنُهُ - قَالَ - فَقُلْتُ مَتَى فَعَلَتْ عَيْنُكَ مَا أَرَى قَالَ لاَ أَدْرِي - قَالَ - قُلْتُ لاَ تَدْرِي وَهِيَ فِي رَأْسِكَ قَالَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ خَلَقَهَا فِي عَصَاكَ هَذِهِ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَنَخَرَ كَأَشَدِّ نَخِيرِ حِمَارٍ سَمِعْتُ - قَالَ - فَزَعَمَ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِي أَنِّي ضَرَبْتُهُ بِعَصًا كَانَتْ مَعِيَ حَتَّى تَكَسَّرَتْ وَأَمَّا أَنَا فَوَاللَّهِ مَا شَعَرْتُ - قَالَ - وَجَاءَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَى أُمِّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَحَدَّثَهَا فَقَالَتْ مَا تُرِيدُ إِلَيْهِ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ قَدْ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَا يَبْعَثُهُ عَلَى النَّاسِ غَضَبٌ يَغْضَبُهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Husayn—meaning Ibn Hasan ibn Yasar—narrated to us: Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Nafi', who said: Nafi' used to say: 'Ibn Sayyad.' He said: Ibn 'Umar said: I met him twice. He said: I met him and said to one of them: 'Do you say that he is he?' He said: 'No, by Allah.' He said: I said: 'You lied to me! By Allah, some of you informed me that he will not die until he becomes the one with the most wealth and children among you, and so he is today, according to what they claim.' He said: We talked, then I departed from him. He said: Then I met him on another occasion, and his eye was swollen. He said: I said: 'When did your eye do what I see?' He said: 'I do not know.' He said: I said: 'You do not know, and yet it is in your head?' He said: 'If Allah wills, He could create it in this staff of yours!' He said: Then he snorted with the loudest snorting of a donkey I had ever heard. He said: Some of my companions claimed that I struck him with a staff I had with me until it broke, but as for me, by Allah, I was not conscious of that. He said: And he came until he entered upon the Mother of the Believers and narrated it to her. She said: 'What do you want with him? Did you not know that he said: "Indeed, the first thing that unleashes him upon the people is anger that enrages him"?'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2933 a, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَا مِنْ نَبِيٍّ إِلاَّ وَقَدْ أَنْذَرَ أُمَّتَهُ الأَعْوَرَ الْكَذَّابَ أَلاَ إِنَّهُ أَعْوَرُ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَيْسَ بِأَعْوَرَ وَمَكْتُوبٌ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ ك ف ر ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'There has been no prophet except that he warned his nation of the one-eyed liar. Behold, he is one-eyed, whereas your Lord is not one-eyed, and written between his eyes is: K-F-R.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2933 b, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، وَابْنُ، بَشَّارٍ - وَاللَّفْظُ لاِبْنِ الْمُثَنَّى - قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا مُعَاذُ بْنُ هِشَامٍ، حَدَّثَنِي أَبِي، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ الدَّجَّالُ مَكْتُوبٌ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ ك ف ر أَىْ كَافِرٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—both saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal has written between his eyes: K-F-R, meaning Kafir.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2933 c, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنِي زُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَفَّانُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، عَنْ شُعَيْبِ بْنِ الْحَبْحَابِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ الدَّجَّالُ مَمْسُوحُ الْعَيْنِ مَكْتُوبٌ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ كَافِرٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ تَهَجَّاهَا ك ف ر ‏"‏ يَقْرَؤُهُ كُلُّ مُسْلِمٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Affan narrated to us: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal has a wiped-out eye; written between his eyes is Kafir'—then he spelled it out: K-F-R—'which every Muslim can read.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2934/2935, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُعَاذٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، - وَاللَّفْظُ لَهُ - حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ رِبْعِيِّ بْنِ، حِرَاشٍ عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الدَّجَّالِ ‏"‏ إِنَّ مَعَهُ مَاءً وَنَارًا فَنَارُهُ مَاءٌ بَارِدٌ وَمَاؤُهُ نَارٌ فَلاَ تَهْلِكُوا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو مَسْعُودٍ وَأَنَا سَمِعْتُهُ مِنْ، رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
en_text: 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us [H]; and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us—and the wording is his: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said concerning the Dajjal: 'Indeed, with him are water and fire; his fire is cool water and his water is fire, so do not perish!' Abu Mas'ud said: 'And I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2934 a, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ نُمَيْرٍ، وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْعَلاَءِ، وَإِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ إِسْحَاقُ أَخْبَرَنَا وَقَالَ الآخَرَانِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ شَقِيقٍ، عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ الدَّجَّالُ أَعْوَرُ الْعَيْنِ الْيُسْرَى جُفَالُ الشَّعَرِ مَعَهُ جَنَّةٌ وَنَارٌ فَنَارُهُ جَنَّةٌ وَجَنَّتُهُ نَارٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, Muhammad ibn al-'Ala', and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: 'informed us', and the other two said: 'narrated to us'—Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal is blind in the left eye, with abundant hair. With him is a paradise and a fire; so his fire is a paradise and his paradise is a fire.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2934 b, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ هَارُونَ، عَنْ أَبِي مَالِكٍ الأَشْجَعِيِّ، عَنْ رِبْعِيِّ بْنِ حِرَاشٍ، عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لأَنَا أَعْلَمُ بِمَا مَعَ الدَّجَّالِ مِنْهُ مَعَهُ نَهْرَانِ يَجْرِيَانِ أَحَدُهُمَا رَأْىَ الْعَيْنِ مَاءٌ أَبْيَضُ وَالآخَرُ رَأْىَ الْعَيْنِ نَارٌ تَأَجَّجُ فَإِمَّا أَدْرَكَنَّ أَحَدٌ فَلْيَأْتِ النَّهْرَ الَّذِي يَرَاهُ نَارًا وَلْيُغَمِّضْ ثُمَّ لْيُطَأْطِئْ رَأْسَهُ فَيَشْرَبَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مَاءٌ بَارِدٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّجَّالَ مَمْسُوحُ الْعَيْنِ عَلَيْهَا ظَفَرَةٌ غَلِيظَةٌ مَكْتُوبٌ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ كَافِرٌ يَقْرَؤُهُ كُلُّ مُؤْمِنٍ كَاتِبٍ وَغَيْرِ كَاتِبٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'I know what is with the Dajjal better than he does. With him are two flowing rivers: one of them, to the sight of the eye, is white water, and the other, to the sight of the eye, is blazing fire. So if anyone encounters him, let him go to the river that he sees as fire, close his eyes, then lower his head and drink from it, for it is cool water. And indeed, the Dajjal has a wiped-out eye over which is a thick piece of flesh; written between his eyes is Kafir, which every believer will read, whether literate or illiterate.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2935 a, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُجْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعَيْبُ بْنُ صَفْوَانَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ رِبْعِيِّ، بْنِ حِرَاشٍ عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ عَمْرٍو أَبِي مَسْعُودٍ الأَنْصَارِيِّ، قَالَ انْطَلَقْتُ مَعَهُ إِلَى حُذَيْفَةَ بْنِ الْيَمَانِ فَقَالَ لَهُ عُقْبَةُ حَدِّثْنِي مَا سَمِعْتَ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي الدَّجَّالِ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ الدَّجَّالَ يَخْرُجُ وَإِنَّ مَعَهُ مَاءً وَنَارًا فَأَمَّا الَّذِي يَرَاهُ النَّاسُ مَاءً فَنَارٌ تُحْرِقُ وَأَمَّا الَّذِي يَرَاهُ النَّاسُ نَارًا فَمَاءٌ بَارِدٌ عَذْبٌ فَمَنْ أَدْرَكَ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمْ فَلْيَقَعْ فِي الَّذِي يَرَاهُ نَارًا فَإِنَّهُ مَاءٌ عَذْبٌ طَيِّبٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ عُقْبَةُ وَأَنَا قَدْ، سَمِعْتُهُ تَصْدِيقًا، لِحُذَيْفَةَ ‏.‏
en_text: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us: Shu'ayb ibn Safwan narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amr Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: I went with him to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and 'Uqbah said to him: 'Narrate to me what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concerning the Dajjal.' He said: 'The Dajjal will emerge, and with him will be water and fire. As for what people see as water, it is burning fire; and as for what people see as fire, it is cool, sweet water. So whoever among you reaches that, let him plunge into what he sees as fire, for it is sweet, wholesome water.' 'Uqbah said: 'And I have heard it as well, confirming Hudhayfah.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2935 b, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُجْرٍ السَّعْدِيُّ، وَإِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، - وَاللَّفْظُ لاِبْنِ حُجْرٍ قَالَ إِسْحَاقُ أَخْبَرَنَا وَقَالَ ابْنُ حُجْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا جَرِيرٌ، عَنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ، عَنْ نُعَيْمِ بْنِ أَبِي هِنْدٍ، عَنْ رِبْعِيِّ، بْنِ حِرَاشٍ قَالَ اجْتَمَعَ حُذَيْفَةُ وَأَبُو مَسْعُودٍ فَقَالَ حُذَيْفَةُ ‏"‏ لأَنَا بِمَا مَعَ الدَّجَّالِ أَعْلَمُ مِنْهُ إِنَّ مَعَهُ نَهْرًا مِنْ مَاءٍ وَنَهْرًا مِنْ نَارٍ فَأَمَّا الَّذِي تَرَوْنَ أَنَّهُ نَارٌ مَاءٌ وَأَمَّا الَّذِي تَرَوْنَ أَنَّهُ مَاءٌ نَارٌ فَمَنْ أَدْرَكَ ذَلِكَ مِنْكُمْ فَأَرَادَ الْمَاءَ فَلْيَشْرَبْ مِنَ الَّذِي يَرَاهُ أَنَّهُ نَارٌ فَإِنَّهُ سَيَجِدُهُ مَاءً ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو مَسْعُودٍ هَكَذَا سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏.‏
en_text: 'Ali ibn Hujr as-Sa'di and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Hujr's; Ishaq said: 'informed us', and Ibn Hujr said: 'narrated to us'—Jarir narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Nu'aym ibn Abi Hind, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: Hudhayfah and Abu Mas'ud met together, and Hudhayfah said: 'I certainly know what is with the Dajjal better than he does. With him is a river of water and a river of fire; as for that which you see as fire, it is water, and as for that which you see as water, it is fire. So whoever among you reaches that and wants water, let him drink from that which he sees as fire, for he will find it to be water.' Abu Mas'ud said: 'This is how I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2936, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ رَافِعٍ، حَدَّثَنَا حُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شَيْبَانُ، عَنْ يَحْيَى، عَنْ أَبِي، سَلَمَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَلاَ أُخْبِرُكُمْ عَنِ الدَّجَّالِ حَدِيثًا مَا حَدَّثَهُ نَبِيٌّ قَوْمَهُ إِنَّهُ أَعْوَرُ وَإِنَّهُ يَجِيءُ مَعَهُ مِثْلُ الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ فَالَّتِي يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا الْجَنَّةُ هِيَ النَّارُ وَإِنِّي أَنْذَرْتُكُمْ بِهِ كَمَا أَنْذَرَ بِهِ نُوحٌ قَوْمَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Shall I not inform you concerning the Dajjal a narration that no prophet ever narrated to his people? Indeed, he is one-eyed, and he will bring with him the likeness of Paradise and the Fire; that which he says is Paradise is the Fire. And indeed, I have warned you of him just as Nuh warned his people of him.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2937 a, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو خَيْثَمَةَ، زُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ حَدَّثَنَا الْوَلِيدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ، بْنُ يَزِيدَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ جَابِرٍ الطَّائِيُّ، قَاضِي حِمْصَ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ، جُبَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ، جُبَيْرِ بْنِ نُفَيْرٍ الْحَضْرَمِيِّ أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ النَّوَّاسَ بْنَ سَمْعَانَ الْكِلاَبِيَّ، ح وَحَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مِهْرَانَ الرَّازِيُّ، - وَاللَّفْظُ لَهُ - حَدَّثَنَا الْوَلِيدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ جَابِرٍ الطَّائِيِّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ، نُفَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ، جُبَيْرِ بْنِ نُفَيْرٍ عَنِ النَّوَّاسِ بْنِ سَمْعَانَ، قَالَ ذَكَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الدَّجَّالَ ذَاتَ غَدَاةٍ فَخَفَّضَ فِيهِ وَرَفَّعَ حَتَّى ظَنَنَّاهُ فِي طَائِفَةِ النَّخْلِ فَلَمَّا رُحْنَا إِلَيْهِ عَرَفَ ذَلِكَ فِينَا فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا شَأْنُكُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ذَكَرْتَ الدَّجَّالَ غَدَاةً فَخَفَّضْتَ فِيهِ وَرَفَّعْتَ حَتَّى ظَنَنَّاهُ فِي طَائِفَةِ النَّخْلِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ غَيْرُ الدَّجَّالِ أَخْوَفُنِي عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ يَخْرُجْ وَأَنَا فِيكُمْ فَأَنَا حَجِيجُهُ دُونَكُمْ وَإِنْ يَخْرُجْ وَلَسْتُ فِيكُمْ فَامْرُؤٌ حَجِيجُ نَفْسِهِ وَاللَّهُ خَلِيفَتِي عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ إِنَّهُ شَابٌّ قَطَطٌ عَيْنُهُ طَافِئَةٌ كَأَنِّي أُشَبِّهُهُ بِعَبْدِ الْعُزَّى بْنِ قَطَنٍ فَمَنْ أَدْرَكَهُ مِنْكُمْ فَلْيَقْرَأْ عَلَيْهِ فَوَاتِحَ سُورَةِ الْكَهْفِ إِنَّهُ خَارِجٌ خَلَّةً بَيْنَ الشَّأْمِ وَالْعِرَاقِ فَعَاثَ يَمِينًا وَعَاثَ شِمَالاً يَا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ فَاثْبُتُوا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا لَبْثُهُ فِي الأَرْضِ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَرْبَعُونَ يَوْمًا يَوْمٌ كَسَنَةٍ وَيَوْمٌ كَشَهْرٍ وَيَوْمٌ كَجُمُعَةٍ وَسَائِرُ أَيَّامِهِ كَأَيَّامِكُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَذَلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي كَسَنَةٍ أَتَكْفِينَا فِيهِ صَلاَةُ يَوْمٍ قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ اقْدُرُوا لَهُ قَدْرَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا إِسْرَاعُهُ فِي الأَرْضِ قَالَ ‏"‏ كَالْغَيْثِ اسْتَدْبَرَتْهُ الرِّيحُ فَيَأْتِي عَلَى الْقَوْمِ فَيَدْعُوهُمْ فَيُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَيَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُ فَيَأْمُرُ السَّمَاءَ فَتُمْطِرُ وَالأَرْضَ فَتُنْبِتُ فَتَرُوحُ عَلَيْهِمْ سَارِحَتُهُمْ أَطْوَلَ مَا كَانَتْ ذُرًا وَأَسْبَغَهُ ضُرُوعًا وَأَمَدَّهُ خَوَاصِرَ ثُمَّ يَأْتِي الْقَوْمَ فَيَدْعُوهُمْ فَيَرُدُّونَ عَلَيْهِ قَوْلَهُ فَيَنْصَرِفُ عَنْهُمْ فَيُصْبِحُونَ مُمْحِلِينَ لَيْسَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ شَىْءٌ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ وَيَمُرُّ بِالْخَرِبَةِ فَيَقُولُ لَهَا أَخْرِجِي كُنُوزَكِ ‏.‏ فَتَتْبَعُهُ كُنُوزُهَا كَيَعَاسِيبِ النَّحْلِ ثُمَّ يَدْعُو رَجُلاً مُمْتَلِئًا شَبَابًا فَيَضْرِبُهُ بِالسَّيْفِ فَيَقْطَعُهُ جَزْلَتَيْنِ رَمْيَةَ الْغَرَضِ ثُمَّ يَدْعُوهُ فَيُقْبِلُ وَيَتَهَلَّلُ وَجْهُهُ يَضْحَكُ فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ بَعَثَ اللَّهُ الْمَسِيحَ ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ فَيَنْزِلُ عِنْدَ الْمَنَارَةِ الْبَيْضَاءِ شَرْقِيَّ دِمَشْقَ بَيْنَ مَهْرُودَتَيْنِ وَاضِعًا كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى أَجْنِحَةِ مَلَكَيْنِ إِذَا طَأْطَأَ رَأَسَهُ قَطَرَ وَإِذَا رَفَعَهُ تَحَدَّرَ مِنْهُ جُمَانٌ كَاللُّؤْلُؤِ فَلاَ يَحِلُّ لِكَافِرٍ يَجِدُ رِيحَ نَفَسِهِ إِلاَّ مَاتَ وَنَفَسُهُ يَنْتَهِي حَيْثُ يَنْتَهِي طَرْفُهُ فَيَطْلُبُهُ حَتَّى يُدْرِكَهُ بِبَابِ لُدٍّ فَيَقْتُلُهُ ثُمَّ يَأْتِي عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ قَوْمٌ قَدْ عَصَمَهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ فَيَمْسَحُ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمْ وَيُحَدِّثُهُمْ بِدَرَجَاتِهِمْ فِي الْجَنَّةِ فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ أَوْحَى اللَّهُ إِلَى عِيسَى إِنِّي قَدْ أَخْرَجْتُ عِبَادًا لِي لاَ يَدَانِ لأَحَدٍ بِقِتَالِهِمْ فَحَرِّزْ عِبَادِي إِلَى الطُّورِ ‏.‏ وَيَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ وَهُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنْسِلُونَ فَيَمُرُّ أَوَائِلُهُمْ عَلَى بُحَيْرَةِ طَبَرِيَّةَ فَيَشْرَبُونَ مَا فِيهَا وَيَمُرُّ آخِرُهُمْ فَيَقُولُونَ لَقَدْ كَانَ بِهَذِهِ مَرَّةً مَاءٌ ‏.‏ وَيُحْصَرُ نَبِيُّ اللَّهُ عِيسَى وَأَصْحَابُهُ حَتَّى يَكُونَ رَأْسُ الثَّوْرِ لأَحَدِهِمْ خَيْرًا مِنْ مِائَةِ دِينَارٍ لأَحَدِكُمُ الْيَوْمَ فَيَرْغَبُ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ عِيسَى وَأَصْحَابُهُ فَيُرْسِلُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهُمُ النَّغَفَ فِي رِقَابِهِمْ فَيُصْبِحُونَ فَرْسَى كَمَوْتِ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ يَهْبِطُ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ عِيسَى وَأَصْحَابُهُ إِلَى الأَرْضِ فَلاَ يَجِدُونَ فِي الأَرْضِ مَوْضِعَ شِبْرٍ إِلاَّ مَلأَهُ زَهَمُهُمْ وَنَتْنُهُمْ فَيَرْغَبُ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ عِيسَى وَأَصْحَابُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ فَيُرْسِلُ اللَّهُ طَيْرًا كَأَعْنَاقِ الْبُخْتِ فَتَحْمِلُهُمْ فَتَطْرَحُهُمْ حَيْثُ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ يُرْسِلُ اللَّهُ مَطَرًا لاَ يَكُنُّ مِنْهُ بَيْتُ مَدَرٍ وَلاَ وَبَرٍ فَيَغْسِلُ الأَرْضَ حَتَّى يَتْرُكَهَا كَالزَّلَفَةِ ثُمَّ يُقَالُ لِلأَرْضِ أَنْبِتِي ثَمَرَتَكِ وَرُدِّي بَرَكَتَكِ ‏.‏ فَيَوْمَئِذٍ تَأْكُلُ الْعِصَابَةُ مِنَ الرُّمَّانَةِ وَيَسْتَظِلُّونَ بِقِحْفِهَا وَيُبَارَكُ فِي الرِّسْلِ حَتَّى أَنَّ اللِّقْحَةَ مِنَ الإِبِلِ لَتَكْفِي الْفِئَامَ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَاللِّقْحَةَ مِنَ الْبَقَرِ لَتَكْفِي الْقَبِيلَةَ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَاللِّقْحَةَ مِنَ الْغَنَمِ لَتَكْفِي الْفَخِذَ مِنَ النَّاسِ فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رِيحًا طَيِّبَةً فَتَأْخُذُهُمْ تَحْتَ آبَاطِهِمْ فَتَقْبِضُ رُوحَ كُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ وَكُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ وَيَبْقَى شِرَارُ النَّاسِ يَتَهَارَجُونَ فِيهَا تَهَارُجَ الْحُمُرِ فَعَلَيْهِمْ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Abu Khaythamah, Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to me: Yahya ibn Jabir at-Ta'i, the judge of Hims, narrated to me: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from his father, Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami, that he heard an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Kilabi [H]; and Muhammad ibn Mihran ar-Razi narrated to me—and the wording is his: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Jabir at-Ta'i, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) mentioned the Dajjal one morning. He lowered and raised his tone concerning him until we thought he was in the cluster of the date-palm trees. When we went to him in the evening, he recognized that in us and said: 'What is the matter with you?' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you mentioned the Dajjal this morning, lowering and raising your tone concerning him until we thought he was in the cluster of the date-palm trees.' He said: 'Something other than the Dajjal is what I fear most for you. If he emerges while I am among you, I will be his adversary on your behalf. But if he emerges while I am not among you, then each man is his own advocate, and Allah is my successor over every Muslim. Indeed, he is a young man with very curly hair, whose eye is floating, as if I would liken him to 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qatan. Whosoever among you reaches his time, let him recite over him the opening verses of Surat al-Kahf. He will emerge from a road between ash-Sham and Iraq, and will wreak havoc to the right and wreak havoc to the left. O servants of Allah, remain steadfast!' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how long will he remain on earth?' He said: 'Forty days: a day like a year, a day like a month, a day like a week, and the rest of his days like your days.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, that day which is like a year, will the prayer of a single day suffice us in it?' He said: 'No, calculate its measure.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how swift will he be on earth?' He said: 'Like a rain cloud driven from behind by the wind. He will come to a people and invite them, and they will believe in him and respond to him. So he will command the sky and it will rain, and the earth and it will bring forth crops. Their grazing herds will return to them in the evening with their humps taller than ever, their udders fuller, and their flanks wider. Then he will come to a people and invite them, but they will reject his word, so he will turn away from them, and they will be stricken with drought, with none of their wealth left in their hands. And he will pass by barren ruins and say to them: "Bring forth your treasures!" and its treasures will follow him like the queen bees of a hive. Then he will call a man brimming with youth and strike him with a sword, cutting him into two pieces severed by an archer's distance. Then he will call him, and he will come forward, his face gleaming and laughing. While he is in that state, Allah will send the Messiah, son of Maryam, and he will descend at the white minaret in the eastern part of Damascus, between two saffron-dyed garments, resting his hands upon the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, droplets fall from it, and when he raises it, beads like pearls cascade from it. No disbeliever who catches the scent of his breath can remain alive, and his breath reaches as far as his eyesight extends. He will pursue him until he catches him at the gate of Ludd and kills him. Then a people whom Allah protected from him will come to 'Isa ibn Maryam, and he will wipe over their faces and inform them of their ranks in Paradise. While he is in that state, Allah will reveal to 'Isa: "I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one has the capacity to fight, so lead My servants to safety at at-Tur." And Allah will send Gog and Magog, and they will swarm down from every elevation. The first of them will pass by the Lake of Tiberias and drink what is in it, and the last of them will pass and say: "There was once water in this." The Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will be besieged until the head of an ox will be better to one of them than 100 dinars is to one of you today. Then the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will beseech Allah, so Allah will send upon them parasitic worms in their necks, and they will fall dead all at once like the death of a single soul. Then the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will descend to the earth, and they will not find a hand-span of space on earth except that their stench and putrefaction fills it. Then the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will beseech Allah, so Allah will send birds with necks like Bactrian camels that will carry them away and throw them wherever Allah wills. Then Allah will send down rain that no house of clay or tent of camel-hair will shut out, and it will wash the earth until it leaves it like a mirror. Then it will be said to the earth: "Bring forth your fruit and return your blessing." On that day, a group of people will eat from a single pomegranate and seek shade under its peel, and milk will be blessed until a milch-camel will suffice a huge gathering of people, a milch-cow will suffice a tribe of people, and a milch-sheep will suffice a family clan of people. While they are in that state, Allah will send a pleasant wind that will take them under their armpits, taking the soul of every believer and every Muslim, and the worst of people will remain, copulating openly like donkeys, and upon them the Hour will be established.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2937 b, book 54, باب ذِكْرِ الدَّجَّالِ وَصِفَتِهِ وَمَا مَعَهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُجْرٍ السَّعْدِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ، وَالْوَلِيدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ - قَالَ ابْنُ حُجْرٍ دَخَلَ حَدِيثُ أَحَدِهِمَا فِي حَدِيثِ الآخَرِ - عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ بِهَذَا الإِسْنَادِ ‏.‏ نَحْوَ مَا ذَكَرْنَا وَزَادَ بَعْدَ قَوْلِهِ ‏"‏ لَقَدْ كَانَ بِهَذِهِ مَرَّةً مَاءٌ ثُمَّ يَسِيرُونَ حَتَّى يَنْتَهُوا إِلَى جَبَلِ الْخَمَرِ وَهُوَ جَبَلُ بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ فَيَقُولُونَ لَقَدْ قَتَلْنَا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ هَلُمَّ فَلْنَقْتُلْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ ‏.‏ فَيَرْمُونَ بِنُشَّابِهِمْ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَيَرُدُّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ نُشَّابَهُمْ مَخْضُوبَةً دَمًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَفِي رِوَايَةِ ابْنِ حُجْرٍ ‏"‏ فَإِنِّي قَدْ أَنْزَلْتُ عِبَادًا لِي لاَ يَدَىْ لأَحَدٍ بِقِتَالِهِمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: 'Ali ibn Hujr as-Sa'di narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir and al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us—Ibn Hujr said: the narration of one merged into the narration of the other—from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, with this chain of narration, the like of what we mentioned, and he added after his saying: '"There was once water in this lake." Then they will march on until they reach the Mount of al-Khamar—which is the mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis—and they will say, "We have killed whoever was on earth, come let us kill whoever is in heaven." So they will shoot their arrows into the sky, and Allah will return their arrows to them dyed with blood.' And in the narration of Ibn Hujr: 'For indeed, I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one has the capacity to fight.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2938 a, book 54, باب فِي صِفَةِ الدَّجَّالِ وَتَحْرِيمِ الْمَدِينَةِ عَلَيْهِ وَقَتْلِهِ الْمُؤْمِنَ وَإِحْيَائِهِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي عَمْرٌو النَّاقِدُ، وَالْحَسَنُ الْحُلْوَانِيُّ، وَعَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، - وَأَلْفَاظُهُمْ مُتَقَارِبَةٌ وَالسِّيَاقُ لِعَبْدٍ - قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي وَقَالَ الآخَرَانِ، حَدَّثَنَا يَعْقُوبُ، - وَهُوَ ابْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ - حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، عَنْ صَالِحٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ، أَنَّ أَبَا سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيَّ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمًا حَدِيثًا طَوِيلاً عَنِ الدَّجَّالِ فَكَانَ فِيمَا حَدَّثَنَا قَالَ ‏"‏ يَأْتِي وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ نِقَابَ الْمَدِينَةِ فَيَنْتَهِي إِلَى بَعْضِ السِّبَاخِ الَّتِي تَلِي الْمَدِينَةَ فَيَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ رَجُلٌ هُوَ خَيْرُ النَّاسِ - أَوْ مِنْ خَيْرِ النَّاسِ - فَيَقُولُ لَهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ الدَّجَّالُ الَّذِي حَدَّثَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَدِيثَهُ فَيَقُولُ الدَّجَّالُ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ قَتَلْتُ هَذَا ثُمَّ أَحْيَيْتُهُ أَتَشُكُّونَ فِي الأَمْرِ فَيَقُولُونَ لاَ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَيَقْتُلُهُ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيهِ فَيَقُولُ حِينَ يُحْيِيهِ وَاللَّهِ مَا كُنْتُ فِيكَ قَطُّ أَشَدَّ بَصِيرَةً مِنِّي الآنَ - قَالَ - فَيُرِيدُ الدَّجَّالُ أَنْ يَقْتُلَهُ فَلاَ يُسَلَّطُ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو إِسْحَاقَ يُقَالُ إِنَّ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ هُوَ الْخَضِرُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ ‏.‏
en_text: 'Amr an-Naqid, al-Hasan al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—and their wordings are close, and the phrasing is that of 'Abd; he said: 'narrated to me', and the other two said: 'narrated to us'—Ya'qub—and he is Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah informed me that Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) narrated to us one day a long hadith about the Dajjal, and among what he narrated to us was that he said: 'He will come while it is forbidden for him to enter the mountain passes of Medina, so he will halt at one of the salt marshes adjacent to Medina. Then on that day, a man who is the best of people—or among the best of people—will come out to him and say to him, "I testify that you are the Dajjal of whom the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) narrated to us!" So the Dajjal will say, "Do you think that if I kill this man and then bring him back to life, you will have any doubt about the matter?" They will say, "No." He said: So he will kill him, then bring him back to life. Then he will say when he brings him back to life, "By Allah, I was never more certain about you than I am right now!" He said: The Dajjal will want to kill him, but will not be given power over him.' Abu Ishaq said: It is said that this man is al-Khidr (peace be upon him).

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2938 b, book 54, باب فِي صِفَةِ الدَّجَّالِ وَتَحْرِيمِ الْمَدِينَةِ عَلَيْهِ وَقَتْلِهِ الْمُؤْمِنَ وَإِحْيَائِهِ
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الدَّارِمِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو الْيَمَانِ، أَخْبَرَنَا شُعَيْبٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، فِي هَذَا الإِسْنَادِ بِمِثْلِهِ ‏.‏
en_text: And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to me: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us, from az-Zuhri, in this chain of narration, the like of it.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2938 c, book 54, باب فِي صِفَةِ الدَّجَّالِ وَتَحْرِيمِ الْمَدِينَةِ عَلَيْهِ وَقَتْلِهِ الْمُؤْمِنَ وَإِحْيَائِهِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ قُهْزَاذَ، مِنْ أَهْلِ مَرْوَ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ وَهْبٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الْوَدَّاكِ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ يَخْرُجُ الدَّجَّالُ فَيَتَوَجَّهُ قِبَلَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَتَلْقَاهُ الْمَسَالِحُ مَسَالِحُ الدَّجَّالِ فَيَقُولُونَ لَهُ أَيْنَ تَعْمِدُ فَيَقُولُ أَعْمِدُ إِلَى هَذَا الَّذِي خَرَجَ - قَالَ - فَيَقُولُونَ لَهُ أَوَمَا تُؤْمِنُ بِرَبِّنَا فَيَقُولُ مَا بِرَبِّنَا خَفَاءٌ ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ اقْتُلُوهُ ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ أَلَيْسَ قَدْ نَهَاكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ تَقْتُلُوا أَحَدًا دُونَهُ - قَالَ - فَيَنْطَلِقُونَ بِهِ إِلَى الدَّجَّالِ فَإِذَا رَآهُ الْمُؤْمِنُ قَالَ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ هَذَا الدَّجَّالُ الَّذِي ذَكَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ فَيَأْمُرُ الدَّجَّالُ بِهِ فَيُشَبَّحُ فَيَقُولُ خُذُوهُ وَشُجُّوهُ ‏.‏ فَيُوسَعُ ظَهْرُهُ وَبَطْنُهُ ضَرْبًا - قَالَ - فَيَقُولُ أَوَمَا تُؤْمِنُ بِي قَالَ فَيَقُولُ أَنْتَ الْمَسِيحُ الْكَذَّابُ - قَالَ - فَيُؤْمَرُ بِهِ فَيُؤْشَرُ بِالْمِئْشَارِ مِنْ مَفْرِقِهِ حَتَّى يُفَرَّقَ بَيْنَ رِجْلَيْهِ - قَالَ - ثُمَّ يَمْشِي الدَّجَّالُ بَيْنَ الْقِطْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ لَهُ قُمْ ‏.‏ فَيَسْتَوِي قَائِمًا - قَالَ - ثُمَّ يَقُولُ لَهُ أَتُؤْمِنُ بِي فَيَقُولُ مَا ازْدَدْتُ فِيكَ إِلاَّ بَصِيرَةً - قَالَ - ثُمَّ يَقُولُ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّهُ لاَ يَفْعَلُ بَعْدِي بِأَحَدٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ - قَالَ - فَيَأْخُذُهُ الدَّجَّالُ لِيَذْبَحَهُ فَيُجْعَلَ مَا بَيْنَ رَقَبَتِهِ إِلَى تَرْقُوَتِهِ نُحَاسًا فَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلاً - قَالَ - فَيَأْخُذُ بِيَدَيْهِ وَرِجْلَيْهِ فَيَقْذِفُ بِهِ فَيَحْسِبُ النَّاسُ أَنَّمَا قَذَفَهُ إِلَى النَّارِ وَإِنَّمَا أُلْقِيَ فِي الْجَنَّةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ هَذَا أَعْظَمُ النَّاسِ شَهَادَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Qahzad, of the people of Marw, narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Abu al-Waddak, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal will emerge, and a man from among the believers will head towards him. The armed guards—the armed guards of the Dajjal—will meet him and say to him, "Where are you heading?" He will say, "I am heading to this one who has emerged." He said: They will say to him, "Do you not believe in our lord?" He will say, "There is no obscurity concerning our Lord!" So they will say, "Kill him!" But some of them will say to others, "Did your lord not forbid you to kill anyone without him?" He said: So they will take him to the Dajjal. When the believer sees him, he will say, "O people! This is the Dajjal whom the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) mentioned!" He said: The Dajjal will order him to be laid out flat, saying, "Take him and wound his head!" So his back and belly will be thoroughly beaten. He said: Then he will say, "Do you still not believe in me?" He said: So he will say, "You are the lying Messiah!" He said: Then it will be ordered that he be sawn with a saw from the parting of his head until he is split between his legs. He said: Then the Dajjal will walk between the two severed halves, then say to him, "Stand up!" and he will stand upright. He said: Then he will say to him, "Do you believe in me?" He will say, "I have only increased in insight concerning you!" He said: Then he will say, "O people! He will not be able to do this to anyone among mankind after me!" He said: Then the Dajjal will seize him to slaughter him, but the area between his neck to his collarbone will be turned into copper, so he will find no way to kill him. He said: So he will seize him by his hands and feet and cast him away, and the people will think that he cast him into the Fire, but he was only cast into Paradise.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'This is the greatest of mankind in martyrdom before the Lord of the worlds.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2939 a, book 54, باب فِي الدَّجَّالِ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا شِهَابُ بْنُ عَبَّادٍ الْعَبْدِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ الرُّؤَاسِيُّ، عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، بْنِ أَبِي خَالِدٍ عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ شُعْبَةَ، قَالَ مَا سَأَلَ أَحَدٌ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ الدَّجَّالِ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا سَأَلْتُ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَمَا يُنْصِبُكَ مِنْهُ إِنَّهُ لاَ يَضُرُّكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ مَعَهُ الطَّعَامَ وَالأَنْهَارَ قَالَ ‏"‏ هُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Shihab ibn 'Abbad al-'Abdi narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Humayd ar-Ru'asi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: No one asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the Dajjal more than I asked him. He said: 'What troubles you about him? Indeed, he will not harm you.' He said: I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they say that with him will be food and rivers.' He said: 'He is more insignificant to Allah than that.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2939 b, book 54, باب فِي الدَّجَّالِ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا سُرَيْجُ بْنُ يُونُسَ، حَدَّثَنَا هُشَيْمٌ، عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنْ قَيْسٍ، عَنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ، بْنِ شُعْبَةَ قَالَ مَا سَأَلَ أَحَدٌ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ الدَّجَّالِ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا سَأَلْتُهُ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَمَا سُؤَالُكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ إِنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ مَعَهُ جِبَالٌ مِنْ خُبْزٍ وَلَحْمٍ وَنَهَرٌ مِنْ مَاءٍ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ هُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Qays, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: No one asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the Dajjal more than I asked him. He said: 'And what is your question?' He said: I said: 'They say that with him will be mountains of bread and meat, and a river of water.' He said: 'He is more insignificant to Allah than that.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2939 c, book 54, باب فِي الدَّجَّالِ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، وَابْنُ، نُمَيْرٍ قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ، بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ أَخْبَرَنَا جَرِيرٌ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ أَبِي عُمَرَ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ، أَبِي شَيْبَةَ حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ هَارُونَ، ح وَحَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ رَافِعٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ، كُلُّهُمْ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، بِهَذَا الإِسْنَادِ ‏.‏ نَحْوَ حَدِيثِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ وَزَادَ فِي حَدِيثِ يَزِيدَ فَقَالَ لِي ‏"‏ أَىْ بُنَىَّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us [H]; and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us [H]; and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us [H]; and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us [H]; and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us; all of them from Isma'il, with this chain of narration, the like of the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Humayd, and he added in the hadith of Yazid: 'So he said to me: "O my dear son!"'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2940 a, book 54, بَاب فِي خُرُوجِ الدَّجَّالِ وَمُكْثِهِ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَنُزُولِ عِيسَى وَقَتْلِهِ إِيَّاهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُعَاذٍ الْعَنْبَرِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنِ النُّعْمَانِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ يَعْقُوبَ بْنَ عَاصِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ الثَّقَفِيَّ، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرٍو، وَجَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ مَا هَذَا الْحَدِيثُ الَّذِي تُحَدِّثُ بِهِ تَقُولُ إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ تَقُومُ إِلَى كَذَا وَكَذَا ‏.‏ فَقَالَ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ - أَوْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ أَوْ كَلِمَةً نَحْوَهُمَا - لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ لاَ أُحَدِّثَ أَحَدًا شَيْئًا أَبَدًا إِنَّمَا قُلْتُ إِنَّكُمْ سَتَرَوْنَ بَعْدَ قَلِيلٍ أَمْرًا عَظِيمًا يُحَرَّقُ الْبَيْتُ وَيَكُونُ وَيَكُونُ ثُمَّ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ يَخْرُجُ الدَّجَّالُ فِي أُمَّتِي فَيَمْكُثُ أَرْبَعِينَ - لاَ أَدْرِي أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا أَوْ أَرْبَعِينَ شَهْرًا أَوْ أَرْبَعِينَ عَامًا - فَيَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ كَأَنَّهُ عُرْوَةُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ فَيَطْلُبُهُ فَيُهْلِكُهُ ثُمَّ يَمْكُثُ النَّاسُ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ لَيْسَ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ عَدَاوَةٌ ثُمَّ يُرْسِلُ اللَّهُ رِيحًا بَارِدَةً مِنْ قِبَلِ الشَّأْمِ فَلاَ يَبْقَى عَلَى وَجْهِ الأَرْضِ أَحَدٌ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ خَيْرٍ أَوْ إِيمَانٍ إِلاَّ قَبَضَتْهُ حَتَّى لَوْ أَنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ دَخَلَ فِي كَبَدِ جَبَلٍ لَدَخَلَتْهُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى تَقْبِضَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ فَيَبْقَى شِرَارُ النَّاسِ فِي خِفَّةِ الطَّيْرِ وَأَحْلاَمِ السِّبَاعِ لاَ يَعْرِفُونَ مَعْرُوفًا وَلاَ يُنْكِرُونَ مُنْكَرًا فَيَتَمَثَّلُ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ فَيَقُولُ أَلاَ تَسْتَجِيبُونَ فَيَقُولُونَ فَمَا تَأْمُرُنَا فَيَأْمُرُهُمْ بِعِبَادَةِ الأَوْثَانِ وَهُمْ فِي ذَلِكَ دَارٌّ رِزْقُهُمْ حَسَنٌ عَيْشُهُمْ ثُمَّ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَلاَ يَسْمَعُهُ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ أَصْغَى لِيتًا وَرَفَعَ لِيتًا - قَالَ - وَأَوَّلُ مَنْ يَسْمَعُهُ رَجُلٌ يَلُوطُ حَوْضَ إِبِلِهِ - قَالَ - فَيَصْعَقُ وَيَصْعَقُ النَّاسُ ثُمَّ يُرْسِلُ اللَّهُ - أَوْ قَالَ يُنْزِلُ اللَّهُ - مَطَرًا كَأَنَّهُ الطَّلُّ أَوِ الظِّلُّ - نُعْمَانُ الشَّاكُّ - فَتَنْبُتُ مِنْهُ أَجْسَادُ النَّاسِ ثُمَّ يُنْفَخُ فِيهِ أُخْرَى فَإِذَا هُمْ قِيَامٌ يَنْظُرُونَ ثُمَّ يُقَالُ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ هَلُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ ‏.‏ وَقِفُوهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ مَسْئُولُونَ - قَالَ - ثُمَّ يُقَالُ أَخْرِجُوا بَعْثَ النَّارِ فَيُقَالُ مِنْ كَمْ فَيُقَالُ مِنْ كُلِّ أَلْفٍ تِسْعَمِائَةٍ وَتِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ - قَالَ - فَذَاكَ يَوْمَ يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ شِيبًا وَذَلِكَ يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from an-Nu'man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Ya'qub ibn 'Asim ibn 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud ath-Thaqafi say: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr—when a man came to him and said: 'What is this hadith that you narrate, saying that the Hour will occur at such-and-such time?' So he said: 'Glory be to Allah'—or 'There is no god but Allah', or a phrase like them—'I was on the verge of never narrating anything to anyone ever again! I only said that you would soon see a momentous matter: the House will be burned, and such and such will happen.' Then he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal will emerge among my Ummah and will remain for 40—I do not know whether 40 days, 40 months, or 40 years—then Allah will send 'Isa ibn Maryam, looking as though he were 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud, and he will pursue him and destroy him. Then the people will remain for 7 years with no enmity between any two individuals. Then Allah will send a cool wind from the direction of ash-Sham, and there will not remain upon the face of the earth anyone in whose heart is the weight of an atom of good or faith except that it will take his soul, even if one of you were to enter the innermost part of a mountain, it would enter upon him until it takes him.' He said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: 'Then there will remain the worst of people, having the lightness of birds and the minds of beasts; they will neither recognize good nor denounce evil. Then Satan will appear to them in human form and say, "Will you not respond?" They will say, "What do you command us?" So he will command them to worship idols, while during that time their provision is abundant and their living is pleasant. Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one will hear it except that he tilts one side of his neck and raises the other. He said: And the first person to hear it will be a man plastering his camels' watering trough. He said: So he will collapse unconscious, and the people will collapse unconscious. Then Allah will send—or he said: Allah will send down—rain like dew or mist—Nu'man was the one in doubt—from which the bodies of the people will sprout. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on. Then it will be said: "O people, come to your Lord! And stop them, for indeed they are to be questioned." He said: Then it will be said: "Bring forth the expedition of the Fire." It will be said: "From how many?" It will be said: "From every 1,000, 999." He said: That is the Day that will turn children grey-haired, and that is the Day when the Shin will be laid bare.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2940 b, book 54, بَاب فِي خُرُوجِ الدَّجَّالِ وَمُكْثِهِ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَنُزُولِ عِيسَى وَقَتْلِهِ إِيَّاهُ
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنِ النُّعْمَانِ بْنِ، سَالِمٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ يَعْقُوبَ بْنَ عَاصِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَجُلاً، قَالَ لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو إِنَّكَ تَقُولُ إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ تَقُومُ إِلَى كَذَا وَكَذَا فَقَالَ لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ لاَ أُحَدِّثَكُمْ بِشَىْءٍ إِنَّمَا قُلْتُ إِنَّكُمْ تَرَوْنَ بَعْدَ قَلِيلٍ أَمْرًا عَظِيمًا ‏.‏ فَكَانَ حَرِيقَ الْبَيْتِ - قَالَ شُعْبَةُ هَذَا أَوْ نَحْوَهُ - قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرٍو قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ يَخْرُجُ الدَّجَّالُ فِي أُمَّتِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَسَاقَ الْحَدِيثَ بِمِثْلِ حَدِيثِ مُعَاذٍ وَقَالَ فِي حَدِيثِهِ ‏"‏ فَلاَ يَبْقَى أَحَدٌ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ إِيمَانٍ إِلاَّ قَبَضَتْهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ حَدَّثَنِي شُعْبَةُ بِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ مَرَّاتٍ وَعَرَضْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from an-Nu'man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Ya'qub ibn 'Asim ibn 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud say: I heard a man say to 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, 'You say that the Hour will occur at such-and-such time.' So he said, 'I was on the verge of not narrating anything to you at all! I only said that you would see a momentous matter shortly'—and that was the burning of the House, Shu'bah said this or something similar. 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal will emerge among my Ummah...' and he conveyed the hadith like the hadith of Mu'adh, and he said in his hadith: '...so that there will not remain anyone in whose heart is the weight of an atom of faith except that it will take him.' Muhammad ibn Ja'far said: Shu'bah narrated this hadith to me several times, and I recited it back to him.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2941 a, book 54, بَاب فِي خُرُوجِ الدَّجَّالِ وَمُكْثِهِ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَنُزُولِ عِيسَى وَقَتْلِهِ إِيَّاهُ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بِشْرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي حَيَّانَ، عَنْ أَبِي زُرْعَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، قَالَ حَفِظْتُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَدِيثًا لَمْ أَنْسَهُ بَعْدُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ إِنَّ أَوَّلَ الآيَاتِ خُرُوجًا طُلُوعُ الشَّمْسِ مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا وَخُرُوجُ الدَّابَّةِ عَلَى النَّاسِ ضُحًى وَأَيُّهُمَا مَا كَانَتْ قَبْلَ صَاحِبَتِهَا فَالأُخْرَى عَلَى إِثْرِهَا قَرِيبًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from Abu Zur'ah, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: I memorized a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) which I have not forgotten since: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'Indeed, the first of the signs to appear is the rising of the sun from its place of setting, and the emergence of the beast to the people in the forenoon; and whichever of the two comes before its companion, the other is right upon its heels shortly thereafter.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2941 b, book 54, بَاب فِي خُرُوجِ الدَّجَّالِ وَمُكْثِهِ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَنُزُولِ عِيسَى وَقَتْلِهِ إِيَّاهُ
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ نُمَيْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو حَيَّانَ، عَنْ أَبِي زُرْعَةَ، قَالَ جَلَسَ إِلَى مَرْوَانَ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ بِالْمَدِينَةِ ثَلاَثَةُ نَفَرٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَسَمِعُوهُ وَهُوَ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنِ الآيَاتِ، أَنَّ أَوَّلَهَا، خُرُوجًا الدَّجَّالُ فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرٍو لَمْ يَقُلْ مَرْوَانُ شَيْئًا قَدْ حَفِظْتُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَدِيثًا لَمْ أَنْسَهُ بَعْدُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏.‏ فَذَكَرَ بِمِثْلِهِ ‏.‏
en_text: And Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Abu Hayyan narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah, who said: Three persons among the Muslims sat with Marwan ibn al-Hakam in Medina and heard him narrating about the signs, that the first of them to emerge would be the Dajjal. Thereupon 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: 'Marwan said nothing; I memorized a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) which I have not forgotten since: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying...' and he mentioned the like of it.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2941 c, book 54, بَاب فِي خُرُوجِ الدَّجَّالِ وَمُكْثِهِ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَنُزُولِ عِيسَى وَقَتْلِهِ إِيَّاهُ
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنَا نَصْرُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الْجَهْضَمِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي حَيَّانَ، عَنْ أَبِي زُرْعَةَ، قَالَ تَذَاكَرُوا السَّاعَةَ عِنْدَ مَرْوَانَ فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرٍو سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏.‏ بِمِثْلِ حَدِيثِهِمَا وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ ضُحًى ‏.‏
en_text: And Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: Abu Ahmad narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from Abu Zur'ah, who said: They discussed the Hour in the presence of Marwan, so 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying... the like of the hadith of both of them, and he did not mention 'in the forenoon'.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2942 a, book 54, باب ‏{‏ قِصَّةِ الْجَسَّاسَةِ ‏}‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ بْنُ عَبْدِ الصَّمَدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْوَارِثِ، وَحَجَّاجُ بْنُ الشَّاعِرِ، كِلاَهُمَا عَنْ عَبْدِ الصَّمَدِ، - وَاللَّفْظُ لِعَبْدِ الْوَارِثِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الصَّمَدِ - حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، عَنْ جَدِّي، عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ، بْنِ ذَكْوَانَ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ بُرَيْدَةَ، حَدَّثَنِي عَامِرُ بْنُ شَرَاحِيلَ الشَّعْبِيُّ، شَعْبُ هَمْدَانَ أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ فَاطِمَةَ بِنْتَ قَيْسٍ أُخْتَ الضَّحَّاكِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ وَكَانَتْ مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرَاتِ الأُوَلِ فَقَالَ حَدِّثِينِي حَدِيثًا سَمِعْتِيهِ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لاَ تُسْنِدِيهِ إِلَى أَحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ فَقَالَتْ لَئِنْ شِئْتَ لأَفْعَلَنَّ فَقَالَ لَهَا أَجَلْ حَدِّثِينِي ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ نَكَحْتُ ابْنَ الْمُغِيرَةِ وَهُوَ مِنْ خِيَارِ شَبَابِ قُرَيْشٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَأُصِيبَ فِي أَوَّلِ الْجِهَادِ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلَمَّا تَأَيَّمْتُ خَطَبَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ عَوْفٍ فِي نَفَرٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَخَطَبَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى مَوْلاَهُ أُسَامَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ وَكُنْتُ قَدْ حُدِّثْتُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ مَنْ أَحَبَّنِي فَلْيُحِبَّ أُسَامَةَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قُلْتُ أَمْرِي بِيَدِكَ فَأَنْكِحْنِي مَنْ شِئْتَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ انْتَقِلِي إِلَى أُمِّ شَرِيكٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَأُمُّ شَرِيكٍ امْرَأَةٌ غَنِيَّةٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ عَظِيمَةُ النَّفَقَةِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَنْزِلُ عَلَيْهَا الضِّيفَانُ فَقُلْتُ سَأَفْعَلُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ تَفْعَلِي إِنَّ أُمَّ شَرِيكٍ امْرَأَةٌ كَثِيرَةُ الضِّيفَانِ فَإِنِّي أَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَسْقُطَ عَنْكِ خِمَارُكِ أَوْ يَنْكَشِفَ الثَّوْبُ عَنْ سَاقَيْكِ فَيَرَى الْقَوْمُ مِنْكِ بَعْضَ مَا تَكْرَهِينَ وَلَكِنِ انْتَقِلِي إِلَى ابْنِ عَمِّكِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو ابْنِ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ - وَهُوَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي فِهْرٍ فِهْرِ قُرَيْشٍ وَهُوَ مِنَ الْبَطْنِ الَّذِي هِيَ مِنْهُ - فَانْتَقَلْتُ إِلَيْهِ فَلَمَّا انْقَضَتْ عِدَّتِي سَمِعْتُ نِدَاءَ الْمُنَادِي مُنَادِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُنَادِي الصَّلاَةَ جَامِعَةً ‏.‏ فَخَرَجْتُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ فَصَلَّيْتُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَكُنْتُ فِي صَفِّ النِّسَاءِ الَّتِي تَلِي ظُهُورَ الْقَوْمِ فَلَمَّا قَضَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم صَلاَتَهُ جَلَسَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لِيَلْزَمْ كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ مُصَلاَّهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَتَدْرُونَ لِمَ جَمَعْتُكُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ مَا جَمَعْتُكُمْ لِرَغْبَةٍ وَلاَ لِرَهْبَةٍ وَلَكِنْ جَمَعْتُكُمْ لأَنَّ تَمِيمًا الدَّارِيَّ كَانَ رَجُلاً نَصْرَانِيًّا فَجَاءَ فَبَايَعَ وَأَسْلَمَ وَحَدَّثَنِي حَدِيثًا وَافَقَ الَّذِي كُنْتُ أُحَدِّثُكُمْ عَنْ مَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ حَدَّثَنِي أَنَّهُ رَكِبَ فِي سَفِينَةٍ بَحْرِيَّةٍ مَعَ ثَلاَثِينَ رَجُلاً مِنْ لَخْمٍ وَجُذَامَ فَلَعِبَ بِهِمُ الْمَوْجُ شَهْرًا فِي الْبَحْرِ ثُمَّ أَرْفَئُوا إِلَى جَزِيرَةٍ فِي الْبَحْرِ حَتَّى مَغْرِبِ الشَّمْسِ فَجَلَسُوا فِي أَقْرُبِ السَّفِينَةِ فَدَخَلُوا الْجَزِيرَةَ فَلَقِيَتْهُمْ دَابَّةٌ أَهْلَبُ كَثِيرُ الشَّعَرِ لاَ يَدْرُونَ مَا قُبُلُهُ مِنْ دُبُرِهِ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الشَّعَرِ فَقَالُوا وَيْلَكِ مَا أَنْتِ فَقَالَتْ أَنَا الْجَسَّاسَةُ ‏.‏ قَالُوا وَمَا الْجَسَّاسَةُ قَالَتْ أَيُّهَا الْقَوْمُ انْطَلِقُوا إِلَى هَذَا الرَّجُلِ فِي الدَّيْرِ فَإِنَّهُ إِلَى خَبَرِكُمْ بِالأَشْوَاقِ ‏.‏ قَالَ لَمَّا سَمَّتْ لَنَا رَجُلاً فَرِقْنَا مِنْهَا أَنْ تَكُونَ شَيْطَانَةً - قَالَ - فَانْطَلَقْنَا سِرَاعًا حَتَّى دَخَلْنَا الدَّيْرَ فَإِذَا فِيهِ أَعْظَمُ إِنْسَانٍ رَأَيْنَاهُ قَطُّ خَلْقًا وَأَشَدُّهُ وِثَاقًا مَجْمُوعَةٌ يَدَاهُ إِلَى عُنُقِهِ مَا بَيْنَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِلَى كَعْبَيْهِ بِالْحَدِيدِ قُلْنَا وَيْلَكَ مَا أَنْتَ قَالَ قَدْ قَدَرْتُمْ عَلَى خَبَرِي فَأَخْبِرُونِي مَا أَنْتُمْ قَالُوا نَحْنُ أُنَاسٌ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ رَكِبْنَا فِي سَفِينَةٍ بَحْرِيَّةٍ فَصَادَفْنَا الْبَحْرَ حِينَ اغْتَلَمَ فَلَعِبَ بِنَا الْمَوْجُ شَهْرًا ثُمَّ أَرْفَأْنَا إِلَى جَزِيرَتِكَ هَذِهِ فَجَلَسْنَا فِي أَقْرُبِهَا فَدَخَلْنَا الْجَزِيرَةَ فَلَقِيَتْنَا دَابَّةٌ أَهْلَبُ كَثِيرُ الشَّعَرِ لاَ يُدْرَى مَا قُبُلُهُ مِنْ دُبُرِهِ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الشَّعَرِ فَقُلْنَا وَيْلَكِ مَا أَنْتِ فَقَالَتْ أَنَا الْجَسَّاسَةُ ‏.‏ قُلْنَا وَمَا الْجَسَّاسَةُ قَالَتِ اعْمِدُوا إِلَى هَذَا الرَّجُلِ فِي الدَّيْرِ فَإِنَّهُ إِلَى خَبَرِكُمْ بِالأَشْوَاقِ فَأَقْبَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ سِرَاعًا وَفَزِعْنَا مِنْهَا وَلَمْ نَأْمَنْ أَنْ تَكُونَ شَيْطَانَةً فَقَالَ أَخْبِرُونِي عَنْ نَخْلِ بَيْسَانَ قُلْنَا عَنْ أَىِّ شَأْنِهَا تَسْتَخْبِرُ قَالَ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَنْ نَخْلِهَا هَلْ يُثْمِرُ قُلْنَا لَهُ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَمَا إِنَّهُ يُوشِكُ أَنْ لاَ تُثْمِرَ قَالَ أَخْبِرُونِي عَنْ بُحَيْرَةِ الطَّبَرِيَّةِ ‏.‏ قُلْنَا عَنْ أَىِّ شَأْنِهَا تَسْتَخْبِرُ قَالَ هَلْ فِيهَا مَاءٌ قَالُوا هِيَ كَثِيرَةُ الْمَاءِ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَمَا إِنَّ مَاءَهَا يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَخْبِرُونِي عَنْ عَيْنِ زُغَرَ ‏.‏ قَالُوا عَنْ أَىِّ شَأْنِهَا تَسْتَخْبِرُ قَالَ هَلْ فِي الْعَيْنِ مَاءٌ وَهَلْ يَزْرَعُ أَهْلُهَا بِمَاءِ الْعَيْنِ قُلْنَا لَهُ نَعَمْ هِيَ كَثِيرَةُ الْمَاءِ وَأَهْلُهَا يَزْرَعُونَ مِنْ مَائِهَا ‏.‏ قَالَ أَخْبِرُونِي عَنْ نَبِيِّ الأُمِّيِّينَ مَا فَعَلَ قَالُوا قَدْ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ وَنَزَلَ يَثْرِبَ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَقَاتَلَهُ الْعَرَبُ قُلْنَا نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ كَيْفَ صَنَعَ بِهِمْ فَأَخْبَرْنَاهُ أَنَّهُ قَدْ ظَهَرَ عَلَى مَنْ يَلِيهِ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ وَأَطَاعُوهُ قَالَ لَهُمْ قَدْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ قُلْنَا نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَمَا إِنَّ ذَاكَ خَيْرٌ لَهُمْ أَنْ يُطِيعُوهُ وَإِنِّي مُخْبِرُكُمْ عَنِّي إِنِّي أَنَا الْمَسِيحُ وَإِنِّي أُوشِكُ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لِي فِي الْخُرُوجِ فَأَخْرُجَ فَأَسِيرَ فِي الأَرْضِ فَلاَ أَدَعَ قَرْيَةً إِلاَّ هَبَطْتُهَا فِي أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً غَيْرَ مَكَّةَ وَطَيْبَةَ فَهُمَا مُحَرَّمَتَانِ عَلَىَّ كِلْتَاهُمَا كُلَّمَا أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَدْخُلَ وَاحِدَةً أَوْ وَاحِدًا مِنْهُمَا اسْتَقْبَلَنِي مَلَكٌ بِيَدِهِ السَّيْفُ صَلْتًا يَصُدُّنِي عَنْهَا وَإِنَّ عَلَى كُلِّ نَقْبٍ مِنْهَا مَلاَئِكَةً يَحْرُسُونَهَا قَالَتْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَطَعَنَ بِمِخْصَرَتِهِ فِي الْمِنْبَرِ ‏"‏ هَذِهِ طَيْبَةُ هَذِهِ طَيْبَةُ هَذِهِ طَيْبَةُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏يَعْنِي الْمَدِينَةَ ‏"‏ أَلاَ هَلْ كُنْتُ حَدَّثْتُكُمْ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّاسُ نَعَمْ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّهُ أَعْجَبَنِي حَدِيثُ تَمِيمٍ أَنَّهُ وَافَقَ الَّذِي كُنْتُ أُحَدِّثُكُمْ عَنْهُ وَعَنِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَمَكَّةَ أَلاَ إِنَّهُ فِي بَحْرِ الشَّامِ أَوْ بَحْرِ الْيَمَنِ لاَ بَلْ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَشْرِقِ ما هُوَ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَشْرِقِ مَا هُوَ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَشْرِقِ مَا هُوَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَأَوْمَأَ بِيَدِهِ إِلَى الْمَشْرِقِ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَحَفِظْتُ هَذَا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
en_text: 'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith and Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to us, both from 'Abd as-Samad—and the wording is that of 'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Abd as-Samad: my father narrated to us, from my grandfather, from al-Husayn ibn Dhakwan: Ibn Buraydah narrated to us: 'Amir ibn Sharahil ash-Sha'bi, of the Sha'b branch of Hamdan, narrated to me that he asked Fatimah bint Qays, sister of ad-Dahhak ibn Qays, and she was among the early emigrant women: He said: 'Narrate to me a hadith that you heard directly from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), attributing it to no one else besides him.' She said: 'If you wish, I shall certainly do so.' He said to her: 'Yes indeed, narrate to me.' She said: 'I married Ibn al-Mughirah, and he was among the best of the youth of Quraysh at that time, but he was struck down in the first jihad with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). When I became a widow, 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn 'Awf, along with a group of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), proposed to me. And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) proposed to me on behalf of his freed slave, Usamah ibn Zayd. And it had been narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever loves me, let him love Usamah." So when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) spoke to me, I said: "My affair is in your hand, so marry me to whomsoever you wish." He said: "Move to Umm Sharik." And Umm Sharik was a wealthy woman from the Ansar who spent greatly in the cause of Allah, at whose house guests would stay. So I said: "I will do so." But he said: "Do not do that, for Umm Sharik is a woman who has many guests, and I dislike that your head covering should fall off or the garment should uncover your shins so that people might see some of you that you dislike. Rather, move to your cousin 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, Ibn Umm Maktum"—and he was a man from Banu Fihr, the Fihr of Quraysh, and he was from the same sub-clan that she belonged to—'so I moved to him. When my waiting period was completed, I heard the caller of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) announcing: "The prayer is in congregation!" So I went out to the mosque and prayed with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). I was in the row of women that directly followed the backs of the men. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concluded his prayer, he sat upon the pulpit smiling and said: "Let every person remain in his place of prayer." Then he said: "Do you know why I gathered you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "By Allah, I did not gather you out of desire nor out of fear, but I gathered you because Tamim ad-Dari was a Christian man who came, pledged allegiance, and embraced Islam, and he narrated to me a narration that agreed with what I had been narrating to you about the False Messiah. He narrated to me that he sailed in a sea vessel with 30 men from Lakhm and Judham, and the waves tossed them about for a month at sea. Then they anchored by an island in the sea just at sunset. They sat in the small rowboats of the ship and entered the island, where they were met by a beast that was hairy and coarse-haired, such that they could not tell its front from its back because of the abundance of its hair. They said: 'Woe to you! What are you?' It said: 'I am al-Jassasah.' They said: 'And what is al-Jassasah?' It said: 'O people, go to this man in the monastery, for he is longing to hear your news.' He said: When it named a man for us, we became terrified of it lest it be a female devil. He said: So we set off quickly until we entered the monastery, and behold, inside it was the largest human being we had ever seen in physical build, and the most severely shackled, with his hands bound together to his neck, and between his knees to his ankles in iron. We said: 'Woe to you! What are you?' He said: 'You have been able to discover my news, so tell me who you are.' They said: 'We are people from the Arabs. We boarded a sea ship and encountered the sea when it was stormy, so the waves tossed us about for a month, then we anchored by this island of yours. We sat in its small rowboats and entered the island, where we were met by a beast that was hairy and coarse-haired, such that one could not tell its front from its back because of the abundance of its hair. So we said: "Woe to you! What are you?" and it said: "I am al-Jassasah." We said: "And what is al-Jassasah?" It said: "Proceed to this man in the monastery, for he is longing to hear your news." So we came to you quickly, terrified of it, not feeling safe that it might be a female devil.' He said: 'Tell me about the date-palms of Baysan.' We said: 'About which aspect of them are you asking?' He said: 'I ask you about its date-palms: do they bear fruit?' We said to him: 'Yes.' He said: 'Beware, soon they will not bear fruit.' He said: 'Tell me about the Lake of Tiberias.' We said: 'About which aspect of it are you asking?' He said: 'Is there water in it?' They said: 'It has abundant water.' He said: 'Beware, soon its water will disappear.' He said: 'Tell me about the spring of Zughar.' They said: 'About which aspect of it are you asking?' He said: 'Is there water in the spring, and do its inhabitants irrigate with the water of the spring?' We said to him: 'Yes, it has abundant water, and its inhabitants irrigate from its water.' He said: 'Tell me about the Prophet of the unlettered: what has he done?' They said: 'He has departed from Mecca and settled in Yathrib.' He said: 'Did the Arabs fight him?' We said: 'Yes.' He said: 'How did he deal with them?' So we informed him that he had prevailed over those of the Arabs near him, and they obeyed him. He said to them: 'Has that really happened?' We said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Beware, indeed it is better for them to obey him. And I am going to inform you about myself: I am the Messiah, and soon I will be permitted to emerge. So I will emerge and travel through the earth, leaving no town without entering it within 40 nights, except Mecca and Taybah; both of them are forbidden to me. Whenever I intend to enter either one of them, an angel meets me with an unsheathed sword in his hand, barring me from it. And indeed, at every mountain pass of it there are angels guarding it.' She said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said, striking the pulpit with his staff: 'This is Taybah, this is Taybah, this is Taybah'—meaning Medina—'Behold, did I not use to narrate that to you?' The people said: 'Yes.' 'For indeed, the narration of Tamim pleased me, as it agreed with what I used to narrate to you about him, and about Medina and Mecca. Behold, is he not in the Syrian Sea or the Yemeni Sea? No, rather from the direction of the East is he, from the direction of the East is he, from the direction of the East is he!' and he pointed with his hand toward the East. She said: 'I preserved this from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2942 b, book 54, باب ‏{‏ قِصَّةِ الْجَسَّاسَةِ ‏}‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ حَبِيبٍ الْحَارِثِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ الْحَارِثِ الْهُجَيْمِيُّ أَبُو عُثْمَانَ، حَدَّثَنَا قُرَّةُ، حَدَّثَنَا سَيَّارٌ أَبُو الْحَكَمِ، حَدَّثَنَا الشَّعْبِيُّ، قَالَ دَخَلْنَا عَلَى فَاطِمَةَ بِنْتِ قَيْسٍ فَأَتْحَفَتْنَا بِرُطَبٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ رُطَبُ ابْنِ طَابٍ وَأَسْقَتْنَا سَوِيقَ سُلْتٍ فَسَأَلْتُهَا عَنِ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ، ثَلاَثًا أَيْنَ تَعْتَدُّ قَالَتْ طَلَّقَنِي بَعْلِي ثَلاَثًا فَأَذِنَ لِيَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ أَعْتَدَّ فِي أَهْلِي - قَالَتْ - فَنُودِيَ فِي النَّاسِ إِنَّ الصَّلاَةَ جِامِعَةً - قَالَتْ - فَانْطَلَقْتُ فِيمَنِ انْطَلَقَ مِنَ النَّاسِ - قَالَتْ - فَكُنْتُ فِي الصَّفِّ الْمُقَدَّمِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَهُوَ يَلِي الْمُؤَخَّرَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ - قَالَتْ - فَسَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ يَخْطُبُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ بَنِي عَمٍّ لِتَمِيمٍ الدَّارِيِّ رَكِبُوا فِي الْبَحْرِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَسَاقَ الْحَدِيثَ وَزَادَ فِيهِ قَالَتْ فَكَأَنَّمَا أَنْظُرُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَهْوَى بِمِخْصَرَتِهِ إِلَى الأَرْضِ وَقَالَ ‏"‏ هَذِهِ طَيْبَةُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ يَعْنِي الْمَدِينَةَ ‏.‏
en_text: Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith al-Hujaymi Abu 'Uthman narrated to us: Qurrah narrated to us: Sayyar Abu al-Hakam narrated to us: Ash-Sha'bi narrated to us, saying: We visited Fatimah bint Qays, and she offered us fresh dates called Rutab Ibn Tab, and gave us barley meal drink to drink. I asked her about a woman divorced three times: where should she observe her waiting period? She said: 'My husband divorced me three times, so the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) permitted me to observe the waiting period in my family's house.' She said: 'Then an announcement was made to the people: "The prayer is in congregation!"' She said: 'So I went along with those of the people who went.' She said: 'I was in the front row of the women, which was directly behind the rear row of the men.' She said: 'And I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) delivering a sermon while on the pulpit, saying: "Indeed, cousins of Tamim ad-Dari traveled by sea..."' and he conveyed the hadith, and added in it: She said: 'It is as if I am looking at the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) as he struck the ground with his staff and said: "This is Taybah," meaning Medina.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2942 c, book 54, باب ‏{‏ قِصَّةِ الْجَسَّاسَةِ ‏}‏
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الْحُلْوَانِيُّ، وَأَحْمَدُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ النَّوْفَلِيُّ، قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا وَهْبُ، بْنُ جَرِيرٍ حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي قَالَ، سَمِعْتُ غَيْلاَنَ بْنَ جَرِيرٍ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، عَنْ فَاطِمَةَ بِنْتِ، قَيْسٍ قَالَتْ قَدِمَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَمِيمٌ الدَّارِيُّ فَأَخْبَرَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ رَكِبَ الْبَحْرَ فَتَاهَتْ بِهِ سَفِينَتُهُ فَسَقَطَ إِلَى جَزِيرَةٍ فَخَرَجَ إِلَيْهَا يَلْتَمِسُ الْمَاءَ فَلَقِيَ إِنْسَانًا يَجُرُّ شَعَرَهُ ‏.‏ وَاقْتَصَّ الْحَدِيثَ وَقَالَ فِيهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَمَا إِنَّهُ لَوْ قَدْ أُذِنَ لِي فِي الْخُرُوجِ قَدْ وَطِئْتُ الْبِلاَدَ كُلَّهَا غَيْرَ طَيْبَةَ ‏.‏ فَأَخْرَجَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى النَّاسِ فَحَدَّثَهُمْ قَالَ ‏"‏ هَذِهِ طَيْبَةُ وَذَاكَ الدَّجَّالُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and Ahmad ibn 'Uthman an-Nawfali narrated to us, both saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us: my father narrated to us, saying: I heard Ghaylan ibn Jarir narrating from ash-Sha'bi, from Fatimah bint Qays, who said: Tamim ad-Dari came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and informed the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) that he traveled by sea and his ship was lost with him, so he landed on an island. He went out onto it seeking water and met a person dragging his hair... and he recounted the hadith and said in it: 'Then he said: "As for me, if permission to come out were given to me, I would tread all the lands except Taybah." So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) brought him out to the people and he narrated to them; he said: "This is Taybah, and that is the Dajjal."'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2942 d, book 54, باب ‏{‏ قِصَّةِ الْجَسَّاسَةِ ‏}‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا الْمُغِيرَةُ، - يَعْنِي الْحِزَامِيَّ - عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، عَنْ فَاطِمَةَ بِنْتِ قَيْسٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَعَدَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ حَدَّثَنِي تَمِيمٌ الدَّارِيُّ أَنَّ أُنَاسًا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ كَانُوا فِي الْبَحْرِ فِي سَفِينَةٍ لَهُمْ فَانْكَسَرَتْ بِهِمْ فَرَكِبَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى لَوْحٍ مِنْ أَلْوَاحِ السَّفِينَةِ فَخَرَجُوا إِلَى جَزِيرَةٍ فِي الْبَحْرِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَسَاقَ الْحَدِيثَ
en_text: Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Al-Mughirah—meaning al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from ash-Sha'bi, from Fatimah bint Qays, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sat on the pulpit and said: 'O people, Tamim ad-Dari narrated to me that some people from his folk were at sea in a ship of theirs and it was wrecked with them, so some of them rode upon a plank among the planks of the ship and emerged onto an island in the sea...' and he conveyed the hadith.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2943 a, book 54, باب ‏{‏ قِصَّةِ الْجَسَّاسَةِ ‏}‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُجْرٍ السَّعْدِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا الْوَلِيدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو عَمْرٍو، - يَعْنِي الأَوْزَاعِيَّ - عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، حَدَّثَنِي أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَيْسَ مِنْ بَلَدٍ إِلاَّ سَيَطَؤُهُ الدَّجَّالُ إِلاَّ مَكَّةَ وَالْمَدِينَةَ وَلَيْسَ نَقْبٌ مِنْ أَنْقَابِهَا إِلاَّ عَلَيْهِ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ صَافِّينَ تَحْرُسُهَا فَيَنْزِلُ بِالسَّبَخَةِ فَتَرْجُفُ الْمَدِينَةُ ثَلاَثَ رَجَفَاتٍ يَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْهَا كُلُّ كَافِرٍ وَمُنَافِقٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: 'Ali ibn Hujr as-Sa'di narrated to me: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Abu 'Amr—meaning al-Awza'i—narrated to me, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'There is no town that the Dajjal will not enter except Mecca and Medina; there is no mountain pass of their mountain passes except that there are angels lined up in ranks guarding it. Then he will alight at the salty barren ground, and Medina will shake with three tremors, whereupon every disbeliever and hypocrite will come out to him from it.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2943 b, book 54, باب ‏{‏ قِصَّةِ الْجَسَّاسَةِ ‏}‏
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنَاهُ أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا يُونُسُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏.‏ فَذَكَرَ نَحْوَهُ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ فَيَأْتِي سَبَخَةَ الْجُرُفِ فَيَضْرِبُ رِوَاقَهُ وَقَالَ فَيَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ كُلُّ مُنَافِقٍ وَمُنَافِقَةٍ ‏.‏
en_text: And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... and he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: 'So he comes to the salty barren ground of al-Jurf and pitches his tent,' and he said: 'and every hypocrite man and hypocrite woman will come out to him.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2944, book 54, باب فِي بَقِيَّةٍ مِنْ أَحَادِيثِ الدَّجَّالِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مَنْصُورُ بْنُ أَبِي مُزَاحِمٍ، حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ حَمْزَةَ، عَنِ الأَوْزَاعِيِّ، عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ، بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ عَمِّهِ، أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ يَتْبَعُ الدَّجَّالَ مِنْ يَهُودِ أَصْبَهَانَ سَبْعُونَ أَلْفًا عَلَيْهِمُ الطَّيَالِسَةُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us: Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah, from his paternal uncle Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Seventy thousand of the Jews of Isfahan wearing Persian shawls will follow the Dajjal.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2945 a, book 54, باب فِي بَقِيَّةٍ مِنْ أَحَادِيثِ الدَّجَّالِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي هَارُونُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ قَالَ ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو الزُّبَيْرِ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ جَابِرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، يَقُولُ أَخْبَرَتْنِي أُمُّ شَرِيكٍ، أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ لَيَفِرَّنَّ النَّاسُ مِنَ الدَّجَّالِ فِي الْجِبَالِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ أُمُّ شَرِيكٍ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَأَيْنَ الْعَرَبُ يَوْمَئِذٍ قَالَ ‏"‏ هُمْ قَلِيلٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu az-Zubayr narrated to me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: Umm Sharik informed me that she heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'The people will surely flee from the Dajjal into the mountains.' Umm Sharik said: 'O Messenger of Allah, where will the Arabs be on that day?' He said: 'They will be few.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2945 b, book 54, باب فِي بَقِيَّةٍ مِنْ أَحَادِيثِ الدَّجَّالِ
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، وَعَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَاصِمٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، بِهَذَا الإِسْنَادِ ‏.‏
en_text: And Muhammad ibn Bashshar and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated it to us, both saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, with this chain of narration.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2946 a, book 54, باب فِي بَقِيَّةٍ مِنْ أَحَادِيثِ الدَّجَّالِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي زُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ الْحَضْرَمِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ، - يَعْنِي ابْنَ الْمُخْتَارِ - حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ، عَنْ رَهْطٍ، مِنْهُمْ أَبُو الدَّهْمَاءِ وَأَبُو قَتَادَةَ قَالُوا كُنَّا نَمُرُّ عَلَى هِشَامِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ نَأْتِي عِمْرَانَ بْنَ حُصَيْنٍ فَقَالَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ إِنَّكُمْ لَتُجَاوِزُونِي إِلَى رِجَالٍ مَا كَانُوا بِأَحْضَرَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنِّي وَلاَ أَعْلَمَ بِحَدِيثِهِ مِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ مَا بَيْنَ خَلْقِ آدَمَ إِلَى قِيَامِ السَّاعَةِ خَلْقٌ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الدَّجَّالِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Hadrami narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn al-Mukhtar—narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from a group of people among whom were Abu ad-Dahma' and Abu Qatadah, who said: We used to pass by Hisham ibn 'Amir on our way to 'Imran ibn Husayn. So he said one day: 'You bypass me to go to men who were no more present with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) than I was, nor more knowledgeable of his hadith than I am. I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Between the creation of Adam and the onset of the Hour, there is no creation greater than the Dajjal."'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2946 b, book 54, باب فِي بَقِيَّةٍ مِنْ أَحَادِيثِ الدَّجَّالِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ الرَّقِّيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرٍو، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ، عَنْ ثَلاَثَةِ، رَهْطٍ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ فِيهِمْ أَبُو قَتَادَةَ قَالُوا كُنَّا نَمُرُّ عَلَى هِشَامِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ إِلَى عِمْرَانَ بْنِ حُصَيْنٍ ‏.‏ بِمِثْلِ حَدِيثِ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ بْنِ مُخْتَارٍ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَمْرٌ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الدَّجَّالِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far ar-Raqqi narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from a group of three from his people among whom was Abu Qatadah, who said: We used to pass by Hisham ibn 'Amir on our way to 'Imran ibn Husayn... the like of the hadith of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Mukhtar, except that he said: 'a matter greater than the Dajjal.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2947 a, book 54, باب فِي بَقِيَّةٍ مِنْ أَحَادِيثِ الدَّجَّالِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، وَقُتَيْبَةُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، وَابْنُ، حُجْرٍ قَالُوا حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، - يَعْنُونَ ابْنَ جَعْفَرٍ - عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ بَادِرُوا بِالأَعْمَالِ سِتًّا طُلُوعَ الشَّمْسِ مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا أَوِ الدُّخَانَ أَوِ الدَّجَّالَ أَوِ الدَّابَّةَ أَوْ خَاصَّةَ أَحَدِكُمْ أَوْ أَمْرَ الْعَامَّةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Hasten to perform deeds before six things: the rising of the sun from its west, or the smoke, or the Dajjal, or the beast, or the private concern of one of you, or the public affair.'

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2947 b, book 54, باب فِي بَقِيَّةٍ مِنْ أَحَادِيثِ الدَّجَّالِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أُمَيَّةُ بْنُ بِسْطَامَ الْعَيْشِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ زُرَيْعٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ رِيَاحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ بَادِرُوا بِالأَعْمَالِ سِتًّا الدَّجَّالَ وَالدُّخَانَ وَدَابَّةَ الأَرْضِ وَطُلُوعَ الشَّمْسِ مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا وَأَمْرَ الْعَامَّةِ وَخُوَيِّصَةَ أَحَدِكُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
